question: Six persons went to a hotel to have their meals. Five of them spent ₹30 each on their meals. The sixth person spent ₹50 more than the average expenditure of all the six. What was the total money spent by all the persons?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The 6th person pays the average amount plus an extra ₹50.

This extra ₹50 compensates for the remaining 5 persons who paid less than the average.

Deficit per person = 50 ÷ 5 = ₹10.

Average expenditure = 30 + 10 = ₹40.

Total expenditure of 6 persons = 6 × 40 = ₹240.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure of 5 persons = ₹30 each

Expenditure of 6th person = Average expenditure of all 6 + ₹50

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of Persons

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the average expenditure of all 6 persons be ₹x.

⇒ Total expenditure of 6 persons = 6x

⇒ Total expenditure = (Expenditure of 5 persons) + (Expenditure of 6th person)

⇒ 6x = (5 × 30) + (x + 50)

⇒ 6x = 150 + x + 50

⇒ 6x − x = 200

⇒ 5x = 200

⇒ x = 40

⇒ Total money spent by all persons = 6x = 6 × 40 = ₹240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average

The average of a given set of numbers is calculated as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

Deviation Method

The net deviation of all values from the average is always zero. If a value is greater than the average, it provides a positive deviation that perfectly balances the combined negative deviations of values strictly lesser than the average.

Combined Average

When combining two separate groups, the overall sum is simply the sum of the individual products of their respective averages and counts. Total Sum = (n₁ × A₁) + (n₂ × A₂).
